title: Transverse callus distraction for the treatment of defect wounds of the lower extremity – a prospective monocentric case series
summary:
This prospective, single-center observational study investigates transverse callus distraction for the treatment of chronic wounds of the lower extremities. Chronic wounds that persist for more than six weeks despite conventional wound therapy and surgical measures are associated with a significant reduction in quality of life and an increased risk of infection and amputation. The aim of the study is to systematically record the efficacy and safety of a treatment protocol for transverse callus distraction used at the study center.
It is planned to include 20 adult patients with a chronic wound on the lower extremity with confirmed arterial blood flow and locally limited infection. All participants will receive the same surgical treatment. A control group is not planned.
In transverse callus distraction, a small bone window is surgically created in the tibia and the bone fragment is moved in a controlled manner over several weeks using an external fixator. The treatment lasts a total of about ten to twelve weeks. Regular clinical follow-up examinations are carried out during this period.
Study-related data collection takes place at three points in time: before the operation, after completion of the fixator treatment, and six months after the procedure. The primary endpoint is complete wound healing six months after surgery. In addition, the time to wound healing, the occurrence of complications and amputations, pain intensity, mobility, quality of life, and satisfaction with treatment are recorded. The results will be used to assess the clinical effectiveness and safety of the treatment procedure at the study center.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•Chronic, therapy-resistant (uncontrollable by conventional wound treatment and surgical measures) defect wound (> 6 weeks) on the lower extremity
•Secure arterial blood supply (at least one patent artery to the foot)
•Locally limited infection (no systemic sepsis)
•Capacity to consent and written consent to participate
•Willingness to undergo and follow up on TCTD therapy
Exclusion criteria:
•Critical ischemia without the possibility of revascularization
•Uncontrolled sepsis or generalized infection
•Malignant tumors or terminal underlying disease
•Severe psychiatric illness or active addiction
•Pregnancy or breastfeeding
•Previous TCTD on the same segment
•Insufficient knowledge of German
